points.t: Intensely **itchy purple flat-topped papules** with fine white lines (**Wickham striae**) on wrists, ankles or lower back; **lacy white patches in the mouth**.
**T-cell attack on basal keratinocytes** (interface dermatitis); hepatitis C and drugs (lichenoid eruptions) are associations.
**Potent topical steroid**, sedating antihistamine at night if needed, review drugs; refer oral, genital, nail or scalp disease.
**Erosive oral or genital LP** (SCC risk), **lichen planopilaris** (scarring hair loss), nail destruction.

cause.lead: An interface dermatitis of skin and mucosa.
points: Idiopathic mostly; **lichenoid drug eruption** (some antihypertensives, antimalarials, gold, TNF inhibitors).
Dental amalgam linked to some oral LP; **HCV** association varies by region.

features.lead: Purple, planar, polygonal, pruritic papules and plaques.
points: **Violaceous, flat-topped, polygonal, itchy** papules ± plaques; **Wickham striae** on the surface.
Sites: **flexor wrists**, lumbar, ankles, shins; genitals.
**Nails**: thinning, ridges, **pterygium**, shedding. **Scalp**: scarring alopecia (lichen planopilaris).
**Marked post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation**, especially skin of colour.

visuals.caption: Lichen planus: flat-topped violet polygonal papules with fine white Wickham striae, and a line of papules along a scratch (Koebner).
visuals.alt: Violet polygonal papules with white lace and a linear Koebner line

visuals.caption: Oral lichen planus: a white lacy network on the inner cheek. Always look in the mouth.
visuals.alt: Inner cheek with white reticular network

points: If uncertain: band-like lymphocytic infiltrate, saw-tooth acanthosis, Civatte bodies.
HCV testing by risk / local guidance; **drug review**.

manage.lead: Skin LP is often self-limiting; mucosal disease needs specialists.

points: Emollients; avoid vigorous scrubbing of the scale.
**Potent / very potent topical steroid ointment** to itchy papules, short courses (caution thin skin).
Stop the culprit drug with its prescriber if lichenoid drug eruption suspected.
Oral, genital, nail, extensive or scalp disease → dermatology / oral medicine: steroid mouth preparations, systemic steroids, phototherapy, immunosuppressants.

items.t: Non-healing oral ulcer, thickening white patch or lump in long-standing oral LP: **refer urgently** (oral SCC).
Genital erosions, scarring or dyspareunia: refer (vulval / penile LP).
Scalp redness with scarring hair loss: early referral (lichen planopilaris).

pearls.t: **Purple, planar, polygonal, pruritic papules and plaques**, and always look in the mouth.
Warn about post-inflammatory pigment lasting months.
Erosive genital itch: examine and refer early.
Document the HCV risk discussion where relevant.

quiz.q: Fine white lines on LP papules?

quiz.a: Flexor wrists, lumbar back, ankles / shins, mouth.

quiz.q: Red flag in long-standing oral LP?
quiz.a: Non-healing ulcer, thickening white patch or lump: urgent referral (SCC).
